question: Who became the first athlete to throw beyond 75 m in the men’s discus event, setting a world record of 75.56 m in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mykolas Alekna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mykolas Alekna**, a prominent **Lithuanian** athlete, etched his name in sports history by becoming the first individual to throw a discus beyond the **75-meter** mark.
 
• In **April 2025**, during a specialized throwing competition, he recorded a phenomenal distance of **75.56 m**, effectively setting a new **World Record** in the men’s discus event.
 
• The record-breaking performance took place in **Ramona, Oklahoma**, a location frequently chosen by elite throwers for its **favorable wind conditions** that aid in achieving maximum flight for the discus.
 
• This achievement broke a barrier that had long been considered nearly impossible to reach, solidifying **Alekna's** position as one of the greatest talents in modern **Track and Field** history.
 
• At the time of this record, **Mykolas Alekna** was representing the **University of California, Berkeley** in collegiate competitions while competing on the international stage for **Lithuania**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Family Legacy in Athletics:**
 
 
• **Mykolas Alekna** is the son of the legendary **Virgilijus Alekna**, who is a **two-time Olympic champion** (**2000 Sydney** and **2004 Athens**) and a former world record contender himself.
 
• Before **Mykolas** broke the record, **Virgilijus Alekna** held the second-longest throw in history with a mark of **73.88 m**, set in the year **2000**.
 
 
 
• **The Previous World Record:**
 
 
• The men’s discus world record was previously held by **Jürgen Schult** of **East Germany**, who threw **74.08 m** on **June 6, 1986**.
 
• **Schult's** record was one of the **longest-standing records** in men's athletics, lasting for nearly **39 years** before being eclipsed by the **75.56 m** mark.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications of the Discus:**
 
 
• In international **senior men's** competitions, the **discus** is a circular plate made of metal or wood with a metal rim, weighing exactly **2 kilograms** (approximately **4.4 lbs**).
 
• The diameter of the men's discus is mandated to be between **219 mm and 221 mm** according to **World Athletics** regulations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 75-Meter Barrier:**
 
 
• Much like the **sub-4-minute mile** or the **9.6-second 100m sprint**, the **75-meter** mark in discus was a significant psychological and physical milestone that had eluded athletes for decades.
 
• Achieving this distance requires a perfect combination of **explosive power**, **rotational speed**, and **aerodynamic precision**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geography of the Record:** The town of **Ramona** in **Oklahoma, USA**, has become famous in the athletics world for "The **Oklahoma Throw Series**," where the open fields and steady **updrafts** provide ideal conditions for records to fall.
 
• **Career Highlights:** Before setting the world record, **Mykolas Alekna** had already secured a **Silver medal** at the **2022 World Athletics Championships** at the age of **19** and a **Bronze medal** at the **2023 World Championships**.
 
• **Competition:** Other top athletes mentioned in the options, such as **Matthew Denny** (Australia) and **Sam Mattis** (USA), are also world-class competitors who have consistently reached the finals of major **Olympic** and **World Championship** events.
